summary.intent: Plan and then execute Phase 69 (FUSE and WinFsp Rust integration with grant-root awareness) end-to-end using the GSD workflow: research, generate executable PLAN.md files, verify them, then auto-advance into wave-based parallel execution.
summary.outcome: All 14 plans were written, verified (plan-checker passed), and committed; execution completed waves 1-3 plus the independent parts of waves 4-5 (10/14 plans merged, core+sdk foundation green), but wave 4's FUSE read-path swap (69-09) uncovered a genuine architectural gap — the write path was never migrated to the new sealed-node format — so the FUSE cutover was halted, and after user approval a researcher+planner pass re-scoped plans 69-09/10/13/14 into a 4-plan atomic cutover sequence (P1-P4), committed but not yet executed.

repo: GSD commit helper has a known false-negative bug: it can report `commit_failed` even when the commit landed cleanly — always verify via `git log`/`git status` before retrying.

Requirements-coverage gates (§13) check the literal requirement ID (e.g. `TEST-03`) in a plan's `requirements:` frontmatter — internal pseudo-IDs like `SC-01..SC-06` don't satisfy the gate even if they map conceptually.

The `intel` plan:pre hook's API-SURFACE regeneration is TS/JS-focused and returns `symbolCount: 0, stale: true` for Rust-only phases — expected, safe to omit from planner prompts when RESEARCH.md already has verified symbol locations.
`crates/core`'s `build_node_aad` fail-closes on non-UUID node IDs — test fixtures across multiple plans (69-06, 69-08) needed real UUIDv5 strings instead of arbitrary test IDs.

Fresh git worktrees for executor subagents lack `node_modules`, which fails the husky pre-commit `lint-staged` hook on first commit — requires `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` inside the worktree before retrying (hit in 69-02 and 69-04).
Running `rustfmt` at the crate root inside a worktree can silently reformat unrelated files — must be reverted/scope-checked before committing (caught in 69-08).
`GET /shares/sent` (`SentShareResponseDto`) has no `revoked`/status field because shares are hard-deleted on revoke — every row returned is inherently an active grant.
The desktop E2E GitHub Actions workflow's real name is "Desktop E2E Tests", not "CI E2E Tests" as the ROADMAP/CONTEXT documented — using the wrong name in `gh workflow run` would 404.
`crates/sdk/src/queue.rs`'s `JournalOp.parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` welds the journal subsystem to the legacy node type — a cross-crate coupling missed by every original FUSE-cutover plan.

The FUSE read/write cutover (SC#1 swap + write-path Node-v3 emission + `InodeKind` flip + `JournalOp` field) is irreducibly atomic across `crates/fuse`, `crates/sdk`, and the desktop crate — a partial/dual-read migration isn't viable; with no prod vaults yet, a clean flag-day cutover is correct (per D-04 greenfield mandate).

code.finding: 69-13 explicitly defers the Windows `spawn_file_meta_reencrypt` caller (line 1183) and the whole-tree SC#2 gate to plan 69-14.

rotate_one's parent_read_key parameter is typed as `&[u8]` (a borrow) specifically so the type system — not just convention — prevents the terminal-owner zeroization rule from being violated by an accidental mutation of the caller's buffer.

workflow: For unattended worktree-isolated multi-plan execution, dispatch the first plan of a wave synchronously as a 'canary' to validate the full executor→worktree→merge→cargo-gate pipeline before fanning out the remaining plans in parallel.

When a planner subagent crashes mid-response (API error), already-written plans persist on disk (filesystem fallback) — recover by spawning a fresh single-plan-mode planner for just the missing plan rather than restarting the whole phase.

Worktree-agent `<worktree_metadata>` can report a mis-captured `expected_base` (e.g. the agent's own docs commit instead of the true fork point) — always verify the actual merge-base via git before recording/merging rather than trusting the self-reported value.

When an executor subagent discovers a genuine architectural scope gap (e.g. a partial migration that would break the build or ship a regression), it should stop and document the gap (deviation Rule 4) rather than attempt an unsafe rewrite — this correctly triggered a human decision point instead of silent damage.
For long-running GSD flows that may span a pause/resume boundary, write a durable handoff file to the scratchpad directory and use ScheduleWakeup so recovery state survives context summarization.

friction: gsd-planner subagent hit an API error (connection closed mid-response) while writing the final plan (69-14) of a 14-plan phase, requiring a manual disk-state diagnosis and recovery.
GSD's commit helper repeatedly reported `commit_failed` for commits that actually succeeded, requiring manual git verification each time (VALIDATION.md commit, phase-plan commit).
Worktree executor agents repeatedly hit husky/lint-staged pre-commit failures due to missing `node_modules` in freshly forked worktrees, adding ~minutes of overhead per affected plan.

Plan 69-09 revealed the original phase-69 plan set had a fundamental scoping defect: the FUSE read-path swap was planned in isolation without realizing the write path was never migrated to the new format and that ~9 additional crates/fuse files plus a cross-crate JournalOp coupling were affected — this wasn't caught by research, pattern-mapping, or the plan-checker, only during actual execution.
A worktree agent's self-reported `expected_base` in `<worktree_metadata>` was incorrect (mis-capture), requiring an extra manual git verification step before merging to avoid a bad merge base.
open_items: Re-scoped FUSE cutover plans (69-09/10/13/14, rewritten as atomic P1→P4 sequence) are committed but awaiting user approval before execution resumes.
69-09's original (pre-rescope) worktree with the standalone SC#6 CI grep-gate commit is preserved unmerged and recoverable if needed.

The SC#6 grep-gate added in 69-06/69-09 uses a placeholder symbol name per the plan-checker's non-blocking warning — needs to be confirmed/replaced with the real crate-private resolve symbol name at build/execution time.
Plan 69-14 (WinFsp/Windows + TEST-03) is marked `autonomous: false` and still requires human verification on an actual Windows machine — not yet executed.
Desktop-crate `CipherBoxFS` construction sites and other cross-crate coupling points flagged in the FUSE-cutover research may need explicit handling in the re-scoped P1-P4 plans.
